caveat: the accuracy comparison rests on a small answered set, so the robust finding is the coverage gap rather than the accuracy difference. Read the outcome counts, not the third decimal.

matcher_alone.what_it_is: leave the abbreviation intact and let candidate generation and ranking pick a concept — no cues, no prior. The most natural objection to building this rung at all.

matcher_alone_min_match_length_2.finding: coverage rises to ~0.90 and accuracy falls to ~0.32. `RA` resolves to C0002893, refractory anemia, in every occurrence — the alphabetical CUI tiebreak — in a corpus where it is room air about 97% of the time. Deterministic, and wrong.
matcher_alone_min_match_length_2.what_it_is: the same baseline with the length floor lowered so it can see two-character tokens at all. At the shipped floor of 3 the matcher never sees `RA`, which flatters the idea.

protocol: cues authored from clinical knowledge, never from the evaluation set; only the sense-name to concept-id binding is fitted, on train, by majority with ties broken on concept id. Reported on test.
question: Do authored anchor cues beat most-frequent sense on held-out data?
